studies.title: Join algorithm × parallelism
studies.question: Which join algorithm and thread count compute the same join with the least energy?

recommendations.label: Hash join · 4 threads
recommendations.text: Keep Hash join · 1 thread: every alternative uses more energy. The closest, Hash join · 4 threads, costs 28% more while running 18% faster.

insights: Fastest is not greenest: Sort-merge join · 8 threads finishes first, but Hash join · 1 thread uses 27% less energy while taking 30% longer.

studies.title: Storage format × compression
studies.question: How much energy does the on-disk format cost when the computation is identical?

recommendations.label: Parquet + Snappy
recommendations.text: Parquet + Snappy cuts energy by 56% versus CSV while running 55% faster.

insights: Parquet (uncompressed) (fastest) and Parquet + Snappy (most frugal) are statistically tied: the difference between them is within measurement noise.
Reading the inputs takes 92% of the energy with JSON lines + Zstd but only 29% with Parquet (uncompressed): the format changes the cost of loading, not of computing.

studies.title: Full scan vs inverted index
studies.question: From how many queries does building an inverted index pay back its energy?

recommendations.label: Inverted index · 1 query
recommendations.text: Keep Full scan (regex) · 1 query: every alternative uses more energy. The closest, Inverted index · 1 query, costs 91% more for a 97% latency cost.

recommendations.label: Inverted index · 10 queries
recommendations.text: Inverted index · 10 queries cuts energy by 67% versus Full scan (regex) · 10 queries while running 65% faster.

recommendations.label: Inverted index · 100 queries
recommendations.text: Inverted index · 100 queries cuts energy by 96% versus Full scan (regex) · 100 queries while running 97% faster.

insights: Full scan (regex) · 1 query is both the fastest and the most frugal exact option at 1 query.
Inverted index · 10 queries is both the fastest and the most frugal exact option at 10 queries.
Inverted index · 100 queries is both the fastest and the most frugal exact option at 100 queries.
Inverted index repays its build energy after about 3 queries: building costs 1.79 J more than the scan's setup, then each query saves 555.53 mJ (per-query costs measured at 100 queries).

studies.title: Batch vs incremental, exact vs approximate
studies.question: How much energy do incremental windows and approximate sketches save, and at what accuracy?

recommendations.label: Incremental panes
recommendations.text: Incremental panes cuts energy by 80% versus Batch recompute while running 78% faster.

insights: Incremental panes is both the fastest and the most frugal exact option.
Incremental + HyperLogLog uses 2.7× the energy of the exact Incremental panes, while erring by 1.9% on distinct users: approximate is not automatically greener.
10 % user sample uses no less energy than the best exact option, Incremental panes, while erring by 15.5% on value sum: here approximation buys accuracy loss, not savings.

studies.title: No index vs B+-tree vs hash index
studies.question: Which index answers the query batch with the least energy, build cost included?

rows.label: No index (full scan) · 100,000 queries
rows.skipped: full scans are capped at 2,000 queries (minutes per run beyond that)

recommendations.label: B+-tree · 1,000 queries
recommendations.text: B+-tree · 1,000 queries cuts energy by 81% versus No index (full scan) · 1,000 queries while running 77% faster.

recommendations.label: Hash index · 100,000 queries
recommendations.text: Keep B+-tree · 100,000 queries: every alternative uses more energy. The closest, Hash index · 100,000 queries, costs 593% more for a 723% latency cost.

insights: B+-tree · 1,000 queries is both the fastest and the most frugal exact option at 1,000 queries.
B+-tree · 100,000 queries is both the fastest and the most frugal exact option at 100,000 queries.
B+-tree repays its build energy after about 149 queries: building costs 0.41 J more than the scan's setup, then each query saves 2.77 mJ (per-query costs measured at 1,000 and 100,000 queries).
Hash index repays its build energy after about 213 queries: building costs 0.57 J more than the scan's setup, then each query saves 2.70 mJ (per-query costs measured at 1,000 and 100,000 queries).
